source.title: Benefit of Interpolation in Nearest Neighbor Algorithms
source.authors: Yue Xing; Qi-Fan Song; Guang Cheng

record.tranche_reason: The study theoretically compares nearest-neighbor prediction risk across interpolation levels, a different method and setting from a deep-network model-size sweep. It reports whether interpolation improves risk and how risk changes as interpolation increases.
record.gate_note: The paper varies interpolation level γ in nearest-neighbor weighting schemes, not deep-network size, training epochs, or sample size near an interpolation threshold. Theoretical risk-ratio results and the reported simulation curves bear on the general double-descent version. Figure 1 and results attributed to other papers are not recorded. The classification instability results do not measure test error and are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study derives and simulates test MSE and regret for inverse-distance-weighted nearest neighbours as the interpolation level γ moves past the non-interpolating kNN point (γ=0). That bears on V4, whether risk improves past interpolation in a non-deep model class. The authors treat γ as a surrogate for complexity; this is their framing, not a parameter count.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that mild interpolation (γ in a d-dependent range, k tuned per γ) strictly lowers the asymptotic multiplicative constant of MSE and regret versus optimal kNN, and improves stability. Risk is U-shaped in γ, with the same ratio for regression and classification. They argue this yields a W-shaped curve that 'predicts' the second U of double descent. They also state that the non-interpolating OWNN does better, and that the gain shrinks in high dimension.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes inverse-distance-weighted nearest neighbors while varying interpolation level γ and derives asymptotic risk ratios; it does not reproduce a deep-network size sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported benefit depends on interpolation level γ, dimension d, and whether k is optimized separately for each γ. The paper states that the benefit diminishes as d grows; γ/d=0.35 in the simulations is outside the theoretical range.

fits_no_version.finding: On five real classification datasets, test error at the best selected γ is slightly below kNN (e.g. MNIST 0.04966 to 0.04656).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Choosing an interpolation level for NN classification can slightly lower test error versus kNN.

fits_no_version.finding: Classification instability ratio converges to sqrt(PR(d,γ)) with optimal k, but exceeds 1 with the same k (Cor 4, Fig 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mild interpolation with tuned k improves prediction stability of NN classifiers.

record.peer_reviewed: SIAM Journal on Mathematics of Data Science
record.problems: The central risk-curve result is asymptotic and depends on smoothness assumptions stated to be stronger than some prior nearest-neighbor conditions. The numerical curves are presented as figures without numerical values or reported uncertainty. The real-data experiments compare kNN with the best selected interpolation level but do not report a full curve.
record.rows_left_out: No additional test-error results relevant to the listed versions were left out. The appendix's Figure 5 concerns MSE and optimal k as n and γ vary but the text reports same-rate convergence and larger optimal k, not a sample-size-induced rise in test error. Classification instability results were omitted because they are not test-error measures.

untested.parts: The classical pre-interpolation U-shape is only argued (kNN/OWNN placed in the 'classical regime'), not measured. Only one model class (nearest neighbours) is examined. γ is not a capacity or parameter count, and there is no interpolation threshold reached by growing capacity.
No deep networks or model-size sweep.
No sample-size sweep near a threshold; Fig 5 varies n only to show same-rate convergence.

missing.what: Benefit of interpolation vanishes as dimension grows: lim over d of min PR equals 1
OWNN (non-interpolating) risk is always below interpolated-NN risk; the asymptotic ratio is given
With the same k as kNN, a gain holds only for γ<γ_x, which depends on the distribution

record.verdict_notes: T3 rather than T2: a new model class with a result on V4. The mapping from γ to model complexity is the authors' analogy; any γ>0 interpolates, so this is not a capacity sweep through an interpolation threshold. The results concern the size of the multiplicative constant only; the convergence rates are identical. Real-data rows report best-γ selections without saying how γ was chosen.

versions.untested_parts: No deep networks or model-size sweep.
No test-error comparison as training sample size increases near an interpolation threshold.

The study analyzes nearest-neighbor weighting schemes as a proxy for complexity; it does not test a range of model classes or establish the classical pre-interpolation U-shaped portion across model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is compared across size, epochs, and sample size.
No systematic test of peak dependence on label noise, multiple peaks, or optimally tuned regularization.
No re-counting of complexity by an effective number of parameters.

rows.subject: interpolated-NN regression estimator
rows.operation_detail: Asymptotically compare minimum MSE over k as interpolation level γ varies, against kNN at γ=0.

conditions.value: Theorem 1 assumptions; γ ∈ [0,d/3); k optimized separately for each γ

rows.value: Converges to PR(d,γ) = [1 + γ²(d+2)²/(d²(d+2−γ)²)]^(d/(d+4)) × [(d−γ)²(d+2)²/(d(d−2γ))]^(4/(d+4)); PR(d,γ) < 1 for γ ∈ (0,γ_d), then rises above 1 when γ > γ_d where permitted. γ_d < d/3 for d ≤ 3; γ_d = d/3 for d ≥ 4.
rows.locator: Section 3.2, Corollary 2 and discussion following it
rows.note: The paper describes the ratio as U-shaped in γ. The result is asymptotic and applies under the stated smoothness assumptions.

relationships.condition: Low dimension (d≤3) with γ>γ_d; and high dimension
relationships.reason: For d≤3 the risk rises above kNN again past γ_d, so the improvement is not monotone in interpolation level (R1, R2). Per the text (Remark 1), the gain vanishes as d→∞.
relationships.display_finding: For d ≤ 3, risk rose above kNN again beyond γ_d, while the interpolation gain vanished as d approached infinity.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Low dimension (d≤3) with γ>γ_d; and high dimension
source_check.reason: Remark 1 establishes vanishing optimal relative gain as d→∞, qualifying the benefit's strength. The low-dimensional comparison applies within γ_d<γ<d/3; its later ascent is compatible with V4 rather than a contradiction.

relationships.condition: Comparison with the best non-interpolating scheme (OWNN), and the same-k comparison
relationships.reason: Text-based (Sec 3.4, Remark 2; no rows). The non-interpolating OWNN always beats interpolated-NN. With a shared k, the gain holds only for γ<γ_x, and stability is worse.
relationships.display_finding: Non-interpolating OWNN always outperformed interpolated nearest neighbors; with shared k, improvement was established for γ < γ_x, while stability worsened.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Comparison with the best non-interpolating scheme (OWNN), and the same-k comparison
source_check.reason: OWNN superiority does not test whether risk descends again after interpolation, and stability is outside V4. Remark 2 establishes a sufficient shared-k interval γ<γ_x, not that improvement occurs only there; that interval still supports a benefit from interpolation.

source_check.notes: The complexity axis is interpolation weighting, with k separately optimized; the classical regime is connected conceptually in Section 3.4. Appendix D's classification display has a minus sign inconsistent with Corollary 2 and its final regression display.

statements.correction: Source header: arXiv:1909.11720v1, 25 September 2019. Corollary 2: separately optimized k; PR(d,γ)<1 for 0<γ<γ_d. Journal review status is not established by this text.
statements.problem: The nearest-neighbor result and tuning qualification are supported, but the supplied manuscript has an arXiv v1 header, not a reviewed SIAM header.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Nearest-neighbor regression and classification under the paper's asymptotic assumptions, with k optimized separately by interpolation level
reader_labels.reason: The reported risk ratios fall below the kNN baseline for a range of γ and then rise, giving a second U-shaped curve in interpolation level (R1, R2); simulations report trends mostly close to theory (R3–R6).
